purpose: Teach: 堅持/不均衡/商会/公訴/報い/困窮/参る/折り合い

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 蓮、研究の信念、本気で、絶対、堅持、絶対、しろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Ren — hold firm to your research convictions. I'm counting on your sincerity.
lines.style: Measured, direct authority. Open with steady eye contact. The weight of expectation settled into each phrase, not forced. Warm underneath the firmness — this is faith, not interrogation.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。研究分野の、本気で、絶対、不均衡、絶対、論文で、絶対、扱っております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm genuinely committed to addressing the imbalances in my research field. Thank you for your confidence.
lines.style: Respectful but not stiff. Slight forward lean — meeting his seriousness with your own. Careful articulation, each word deliberate. The gratitude is quiet, real.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 歴史ある、本気で、絶対、商会、絶対、の研究、絶対、進めろ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Push forward with your research on these historic trading companies. That work matters.
lines.style: Clear directive, not harsh. Slight edge of conviction on 'matters' — he knows why this work is important even if you're still finding out. Expects you to understand without spelling it out.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。歴史上の、本気で、絶対、公訴、絶対、事件、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I've addressed historical prosecution cases in my papers — focusing on support systems for researchers facing institutional hardship. Thank you for the opportunity.
lines.style: Methodical recitation with underlying care. You're showing him what you've done, but carefully — not boasting, offering proof. Voice steady, slightly formal in register.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: お前の努力の、本気で、絶対、報い、絶対、必ず、絶対、あるぞ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Your effort will be rewarded. You have my word on that.
lines.style: Quieter intensity. Lean back slightly — the confidence doesn't need volume. Weight of promise in the final phrase. This is not empty encouragement; it's a man keeping score of what matters.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。困窮、本気で、絶対、する、絶対、研究者の支援、絶対、論文で、扱いました、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I've focused my work on supporting researchers facing systemic obstacles, and I'm bringing those findings to my papers. Thank you for believing in this direction.
lines.style: Thoughtful, building momentum through the answer. You're connecting the dots for him — showing how his guidance shaped your work. Gratitude lands warmly at the close, not performative.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_boss
lines.jp: 教授には、本気で、絶対、自ら、絶対、参る、絶対、よう、絶対、頼むぞ、本気で、頼んだぞ
lines.en: Make sure you approach your advisor directly with respect. Don't let anything get lost in translation.
lines.style: Sharp pivot to practical urgency. Short, clean delivery. The final phrase carries warning wrapped in wisdom — he knows what can go wrong when communication breaks down.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい。指導教授と、本気で、絶対、折り合い、絶対、つけて、絶対、研究、絶対、進めております、本気で、感謝
lines.en: Yes. I'm working closely with my supervisor to align our expectations and keep the research moving forward. Thank you for your guidance.
lines.style: Assured closure. You've heard the warning and you're ahead of it — the confidence in your voice says you've already got this handled. Warm gratitude, the real kind that comes from understanding what was just asked.
